title: Payroll Coordinator
description:
Portfolio Payroll is proud to be recruiting on behalf of a well-established manufacturing business based in Manchester. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Payroll professional to join a stable and growing organisation that truly values its people.

Reporting to the Personnel Manager you will take responsibility for the day-to-day processing of the company payroll, ensuring accuracy, compliance and timely delivery.

Key Responsibilities:
Administer payroll for existing employees, new starters and leavers
Maintain accurate and efficient payroll records
Calculate overtime, sickness and statutory payments (SSP, SMP, SPP etc.)
Manage RTI submissions and ensure compliance with auto-enrolment legislation
Ensure payroll deadlines are consistently met and thoroughly checked
Liaise with the People Team and Finance to ensure smooth payroll operations
Act as the first point of contact for payroll-related queries
Produce routine and ad-hoc payroll reporting
Support with additional duties as required

About You:
Proven payroll experience
Strong attention to detail and organisational skills
Up-to-date knowledge of payroll legislation
Ability to work accurately to strict deadlines
Strong communication skills and a collaborative approach

Whats on offer:
- Salary up to £28,000
- Bonus scheme
- Study support to support your professional development
- On-site parking
- Hybrid working

If you're looking to join a reputable manufacturing business offering stability, career progression and study support, and this could be the perfect next step please apply or call and ask for Lidya.

title: Experienced HR Administrator
description:
Experienced HR Administrator

Sale, Manchester M33

14.50 - 16.99 per hour (Depending on Level of Experience)

Monday - Friday

8am-3.30pm

ASAP - 4-month role

Our client, a prominent organisation within the Education sector, is seeking an Experienced HR Administrator to join their dynamic team. This is an exciting opportunity for an individual with a strong HR background to make a significant impact in a supportive and engaging environment.

Key Responsibilities:

As an Experienced HR Administrator, you will play a vital role in ensuring the smooth operation of HR functions. Your day-to-day tasks will include:
- Undertaking routine clerical duties including typing, photocopying and data input across various databases.
- Utilising Microsoft Office 365 packages, such as Outlook, Word, Excel, Publisher, Planner and SharePoint.
- Supporting the communication strategy by cohesive and clear messages ahead of key events, ensuring clarity and professionalism in all communications.
- Maintaining and updating intranet content and communication platforms to ensure that information remains accurate, accessible and current.
- Collaborating with the admin team to coordinate a central meeting schedule and manage logistics for key events.
- Taking high-quality notes during meetings as required.
- Booking and confirming travel arrangements for the central team when attending conferences and training sessions.
- Working closely with the central People and Culture team to manage HR casework, ensuring adherence to correct procedures for staff absence, grievance and capability issues.
- Maintaining accurate, confidential records in accordance with GDPR and data protection legislation.
- Providing administrative support.

Requirements:
- Proven experience in an HR administrative role is essential.
- Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office 365 applications.
- Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.
- Ability to maintain confidentiality and manage sensitive information.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks effectively.
- A collaborative mindset and the ability to build relationships with various stakeholders.

This role offers a unique chance to contribute to the educational landscape while developing your HR career in a rewarding environment. If you are passionate about HR and education, this is the position for you!

title: Healthcare Learning & Development Coordinator
company: Find Recruitment Group LTD - Agency - Permanent
description:
FIND are a specialist staffing business, servicing the Skills & Learning markets across the UK. We are on the hunt for a Learning & Development Coordinator to join a leading care home group.

As the UK's only large care home provider to achieve B Corp certification, our client continue to lead the sector in responsible, values-driven care.
For eight consecutive years, we've been recognised among the Top 20 Large UK Care Home Groups by (url removed), reflecting consistently high standards and resident satisfaction.

About the role

As a Learning and Development Coordinator, you will design, plan, and deliver a comprehensive range of training programmes to ensure our teams deliver high-quality, person-centred care.

You will coordinate learning and development across our residential and nursing care homes (and potentially homecare branches), predominantly in the North West.

As part of your responsibility you will cover mandatory training including: Moving and Assisting, Safeguarding, First Aid, and Basic Life Support, as well as advanced subjects like the Mental Capacity Act and Dementia care. You will also support induction training in new services, develop home-based champions, and carry out supervisions to maintain training standards.

Key duties and responsibilities
- Design, plan and deliver a wide range of training courses, including but not limited to Safeguarding, Moving and Assisting, First Aid, Dementia and the Mental Capacity Act
- Deliver high-quality training to groups of employees across multiple sites
- Conduct learner assessments and ensure outcomes meet Skills for Care and CQC standards
- Support induction training for new homes and employees, ensuring consistent delivery
- Facilitate and lead Champion programmes, supporting home champions to achieve required standards
- Maintain accurate training records and adapt to varying operational needs
- Provide guidance and troubleshooting support on the e-learning system
- Keep training content and methods current and aligned with best practices and Kingsley's ethos.

Skills and attributes
- Proven experience in delivering care-related training across varied subjects is essential
- Excellent communication, presentation and organisational skills
- Strong knowledge of regulatory frameworks in care (e.g. Skills for Care, CQC)
- Compassionate, empathetic, and able to engage a wide range of learners
- Confident using Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint
- Flexible and able to travel between sites as required
- Experience in designing new course content as required

Education and qualification
- L3 Award in Education and Training (or equivalent recognised teaching/training qualification) is essential
- Up-to-date knowledge and experience in delivering subjects including Safeguarding, Moving and Assisting, First Aid and Basic Life Support is essential
- NUCO and RoSPA qualifications desirable.

title: Part-time Recruitment Administrator
description:
As a Part-Time Recruitment Administrator in Manchester, you will keep recruitment administration organised within the Human Resources department of a Business Services organisation. You will manage day-to-day coordination tasks that help the hiring process run smoothly and keep information accurate.

Client Details

The organisation operates in the Business Services industry in Manchester.

Description
- Coordinate recruitment administration to keep hiring activity organised and on track.
- Maintain accurate candidate and vacancy records for clear, up-to-date information.
- Prepare recruitment documents and correspondence to support consistent processes.
- Monitor recruitment inboxes and respond to routine queries in a timely manner.
- Supporting candidates payroll.
- Track key stages of the recruitment process and flag outstanding actions.
- Work closely with the Resources team to ensure recruitment activity is well coordinated.

Profile

A successful 'Part-Time Recruitment Administrator' should have:
- Experience of recruitment administration and coordinating hiring activities.
- Confidence arranging interviews and managing interview communications.
- Strong accuracy when maintaining candidate and vacancy records.
- Ability to manage documents, inboxes and routine recruitment queries.
- Good organisation when tracking several recruitment tasks at once.
- Clear written communication for candidate and internal correspondence.

Job Offer
- Permanent, part-time contract.
- Salary of 25,000 to 27,500 dependent on the level of experience.
- Office based role.

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

title: Recruiter I - 110763
description:
Location: Manchester
Duration: 6 Months
Working Pattern: Hybrid (4 days onsite, 1 day remote)

About the Opportunity

We're looking for a proactive and highly organised Recruitment Coordinator to join a busy talent acquisition team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone at the early stages of their career who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment, thrives on organisation, and takes pride in delivering a great candidate experience.

This role would suit someone who is a quick learner, enjoys managing multiple priorities, and has strong attention to detail. Success in this position comes from being able to work accurately under pressure, maintain high standards, and communicate professionally with candidates and stakeholders.

What You'll Be Doing
- Coordinating interview schedules across multiple hiring processes
- Managing interview communications and ensuring candidates receive timely updates
- Drafting and issuing offer letters accurately and efficiently
- Supporting onboarding activities, including background screening and pre-employment checks
- Monitoring recruitment workflows and ensuring key milestones are completed on time
- Maintaining accurate records and updating recruitment systems
- Responding to candidate and stakeholder queries in a professional and timely manner
- Taking ownership of actions and ensuring tasks are completed to agreed deadlines
- Supporting recruitment projects and other administrative activities as required

What We're Looking For

We're interested in individuals who can demonstrate:
- Strong organisational and time management skills
- Excellent attention to detail with the ability to produce accurate work
- Confidence managing multiple tasks in a high-volume environment
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- A proactive approach and willingness to learn
- The ability to work with urgency while maintaining quality and accuracy
- Professionalism when interacting with candidates and internal stakeholders
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word and Excel

Qualifications and Experience
- Degree qualification or equivalent relevant experience
- Previous experience in administration, coordination, customer service, recruitment support, HR administration, or a similar office-based environment would be beneficial
- Experience working in a fast-paced environment where prioritisation and accuracy are important

What's Important for Success

This role requires someone who can learn quickly, stay organised when managing competing priorities, and maintain a high level of accuracy. You'll be supporting a recruitment function with multiple moving parts, so attention to detail, accountability, and a commitment to providing an excellent candidate experience are essential.
